# Caching Strategies for Web Services

Caching is the cheapest way to make a service faster, but it is also an easy way to serve stale data. This article compares the common approaches and shows how to pick between them. For a longer treatment see the [full caching guide](https://example.com/docs/caching-guide).

## Choosing a strategy

The right strategy depends on how often the data changes, how costly a miss is, and how much staleness your users will tolerate. Start by measuring your hit ratio before you add any complexity, because many services find that a small time-to-live on a single layer is all they need.

- Cache-aside keeps the application in control of reads and writes.
- Write-through updates the cache and the store together.
- Write-behind batches writes for throughput at the cost of durability.

Finally, remember to monitor evictions. A cache that evicts constantly is a cache that is too small, and no amount of clever invalidation will fix that.
